cases.prompt: I am a new backend engineer joining the Orders service. Build a first-week onboarding path so I can run the service locally, understand its boundaries, and choose a safe first task.

setup.title: Orders service local development
setup.snippet: Install dependencies and run the development stack.

get_article.title: Orders service local development
get_article.body: Install the documented dependencies and start the local development stack.

get_article.title: Orders service pull request workflow
get_article.body: Run the Orders test suite and request review from the service team.

get_question.title: Which systems own Orders state?
get_question.body: Orders owns order lifecycle state; Payments owns payment authorization.

get_question.title: Good first tasks in Orders
get_question.body: Start with a documented test-only issue labeled good-first-task.

cases.expected: Identify the learner, first-week goal, and time horizon. Use focused search and strongest-first full retrieval before relying on each source. Produce all five template sections, citing Orders service local development (ID: a-101), Which systems own Orders state? (ID: q-102), Orders service pull request workflow (ID: a-103), and Good first tasks in Orders (ID: q-104) for their supported items. Mark prerequisites as Missing coverage when no retrieved source supports one; do not invent one. Inference: None.

cases.prompt: I am transferring from the Web Platform team to Payments. I have two weeks to learn the payment authorization flow, its release process, and the first support rotation task.

workflows.title: How does Payments release authorization changes?

get_article.title: Payments authorization architecture
get_article.body: Payments owns authorization orchestration and calls the gateway adapter.

get_article.title: Payments support rotation handbook
get_article.body: Begin rotation by triaging the authorization queue with the on-call runbook.

get_question.title: How does Payments release authorization changes?
get_question.body: Authorization changes require the staged Payments release checklist.

cases.expected: State the transferring engineer, authorization-and-rotation goal, and two-week horizon. Cite Payments authorization architecture (ID: a-201), How does Payments release authorization changes? (ID: q-202), and Payments support rotation handbook (ID: a-203) only after full retrieval. Keep prerequisites and setup as clearly labeled Missing coverage when no source establishes them; do not fill them from public payments knowledge. Inference: None.
